status: post-outcome sensitivity diagnostic; not prospective confirmation and not a rescue test

fixed_estimator.session_centering: subtract full retained track median Height
fixed_estimator.self_profile_weighting: equal eligible training track of target individual
fixed_estimator.other_profile_weighting: pool tracks within each other individual then equal-weight other individuals
fixed_estimator.common_weighting: identical self-derived common-cell weights for self and other profiles

only_varied_parameter.name: minimum_presence_qualified_fixes_per_session
only_varied_parameter.interpretation: 0 means no minimum track-length eligibility filter beyond required nonblank fields; all target sessions still require at least 50 scored common-support events

threshold_0.role: revised-eligibility analysis already opened before this diagnostic

frozen_reporting.primary_diagnostic: report calibrated excess at every threshold and whether its sign is positive; no threshold is selected as primary based on p-value
secondary_descriptives: null SD and one-sided permutation p
range and median of calibrated excess
number of thresholds with positive calibrated excess
forbidden_interpretations: do not relabel any sensitivity threshold as a prospective replication
do not choose the threshold with the smallest p-value
do not treat p<=0.05 frequency across thresholds as multiplicity-corrected evidence
do not alter grids, vertical bins, target-event minimum, cohort definition, weighting, permutation unit, B or seed after results

claim_boundary: This diagnostic asks whether the Nyctalus effect direction and magnitude are fragile to the session-length eligibility rule.
The original >=50-fix prospective result remains the confirmatory external test and remains FAIL at its frozen threshold.
A stable positive sensitivity curve may support directional convergent evidence but cannot restore prospective status.
A highly irregular or sign-changing curve would show eligibility sensitivity and weaken the revised-eligibility interpretation.
